stem: An 8-year-old boy with severe asthma has had frequent attacks over winter, was recently discharged from PICU after a severe exacerbation, wakes at night most nights, has exercise-induced wheeze, and uses Ventolin at least daily. If his symptoms get worse, what reliever dose would you prescribe?

options.text: Ventolin 2 puffs up to every 4hrs as needed
Ventolin 6 puffs up to every 4hrs as needed
Ventolin 12 puffs up to every 4hrs as needed

explanation: For worsening asthma symptoms, the appropriate reliever in a standard paediatric action plan is salbutamol (Ventolin) 2 puffs as needed, with frequency up to every 4 hours depending on symptoms. The higher scheduled doses or more frequent dosing shown in the other options are not standard reliever instructions for this scenario.
rationale: The question is asking for the reliever dose in a worsening-asthma action plan. Among the preserved options, 2 puffs PRN is the only standard reliever instruction.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is the standard as-needed reliever dose in a paediatric asthma action plan.
optionExplanations.B: Too high for a routine reliever dose in this action-plan context.
optionExplanations.C: Excessive for standard home reliever use.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because reliever therapy is not given on a fixed 12-hour schedule.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because reliever therapy is not given on a fixed 12-hour schedule.
optionExplanations.F: Incorrect because reliever therapy is not given on a fixed 12-hour schedule.
optionExplanations.G: Too frequent and not the standard written action-plan dose.
optionExplanations.H: Too frequent and not the standard written action-plan dose.
optionExplanations.I: Too frequent and not the standard written action-plan dose.
